CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Anderson is a 44-year-old female presenting with left shoulder pain that began one week ago during a gymnastics class. The patient reports falling or toppling into an awkward position during a move, after which she developed left shoulder pain. She describes the pain as constant and exacerbated by any movement of the left shoulder, including forward and backward motion. The patient attempted self-treatment with Tylenol for two to three days without significant relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain with all movements of the left shoulder.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Previous surgery on the left arm.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (used for 2-3 days without relief).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in gymnastics.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient demonstrates pain with movement of the left shoulder in multiple directions.

RESULTS
X-ray of left shoulder: No fracture or broken bone identified.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Probable left shoulder joint injury/strain secondary to trauma. Plan includes: ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily for one week; alternative pain relief with Advil or Aleve as needed; ice or heat pad application for symptom relief; rest of the left arm for 3-4 weeks with avoidance of heavy lifting and preferential use of right arm for activities; follow-up appointment in 3 weeks; repeat imaging to be considered at follow-up visit if pain persists.
